channel.title: USA AI Monitor
channel.description: AI monitoring of US political, economic and security developments

item.title: The family of Renee Good files lawsuits over her death during Minneapolis ICE raids
item.description: The fatal shooting of Renee Good by a federal immigration agent last January in Minneapolis set off a firestorm of protests around the U.S. Her family is speaking out for the first time.

item.title: 'It's a nightmare.' Former refugee, professor on Trump's new Medicaid policy
item.description: Starting Oct. 1, many immigrants who are here legally lose their Medicaid coverage because of the Republican budget bill passed last year.

item.title: A judge permanently dismisses former Olympian's Reflecting Pool charges
item.description: Citing "exceptional circumstances," a D.C. judge has ruled that the federal government cannot refile its Reflecting Pool charges against David Hearn, despite pressure from President Trump to do so.

item.title: Cornell Jane Doe's attorney says she told police in 2024: 'I was raped'
item.description: Counter to what a local prosecutor has claimed, the alleged victim of a 2024 gang rape at Cornell University clearly said in her police statement that she was sexually assaulted, her attorney told NPR.

item.title: Hasan Piker vows he will pressure James Talarico to govern as a leftist, not a moderate
item.description: Hasan Piker vowed to pressure James Talarico to govern as a leftist if elected, not a moderate Democrat, raising questions about the Texas Senate race.

item.title: GREGG JARRETT: My mother’s advice led me to the career of a lifetime
item.description: Former trial lawyer Gregg Jarrett reflects on leaving his legal career behind and finding purpose during nearly 25 years at the network's news operation.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Supreme Court prayer grotto case could impact 'every single zoning law' in America, attorney says
item.description: The Supreme Court agreed to hear a Kentucky Catholic church's fight over a prayer grotto, a case that could reshape RLUIPA zoning law nationwide.

item.title: Michigan decision forces removal of disgraced sports doctor Larry Nassar from sex offender registry
item.description: Larry Nassar was removed from the Michigan Sex Offender Registry after a state Supreme Court ruling barred retroactive application of registry laws.

item.title: Sleeper Senate race emerges as unexpected headache for Republicans ahead of midterms
item.description: JD Vance rallied for Roger Marshall as the Kansas Senate race against Adam Hamilton tightens with Election Day political headwinds battering the GOP.

item.title: Renée Good’s family sues Trump officials, saying death was ‘not an accident’
item.description: The death of the mother of three sparked protests and scrutiny over how federal officers are using force against both immigrants and protesters.

item.title: Supreme Court to scrutinize ICE’s mandatory detention policy for immigrants
item.description: The case, one of the first the court has accepted since its summer recess ended, promises to be among the most consequential of the term that begins next week.

item.title: Watchdog finds Fed mishandled renovations that Trump tried to oust Powell over
item.description: The Fed’s watchdog found cost overruns but no evidence of criminal violations after the Justice Department dropped an investigation into the renovations earlier this year.

item.title: Democrats fail to stop Trump from canceling $810M in funds approved by Congress
item.description: Sen. Ron Johnson (R-Wisconsin) blocked the effort, meaning the Trump administration will succeed in eliminating the funding it deemed “wasteful.”

item.title: Hegseth bars military academies from hiring civilians as tenured professors
item.description: The move marks the latest effort by the Trump administration to exert more control over faculty at service academies.

item.title: Fearing AI, workers go back to school seeking jobs that still need a human touch
item.description: Some people are abandoning office jobs for teaching, health care and the trades. But switching to the new paths can come with trade-offs.

item.title: Trump embarks on rally blitz, hoping to energize GOP voters
item.description: Trump’s low standing with voters limits the places he can most effectively campaign. Advisers hope he can energize GOP voters.

item.title: Trump illegally fired Seattle’s U.S. attorney, judge rules
item.description: The ruling is the latest in a string of decisions finding that the administration bent federal law to keep loyalists in key prosecutorial posts.

item.title: DOJ charges Boston man with threatening conservative podcaster Katie Miller
item.description: Federal authorities on Thursday charged a Boston-area man with harassing Katie Miller, a conservative podcaster and wife of Trump aide Stephen Miller.

item.title: Trump defies Democrats, diverts aid for Europe to Latin America instead
item.description: The diverted funds include tens of millions of dollars that Congress approved for countries affected by the war in Ukraine.

item.title: Democrats sue over Pentagon’s changes to voter forms for Americans overseas
item.description: Advocates for U.S. citizens overseas say the changes may spark confusion among eligible voters abroad and local election offices.
